intention: Dashboard 'Odometer history' and 'Battery history' cards render responsive SVG bar charts for the selected vehicle over a user-chosen window (default 6 days; presets 6/14/30). Odometer bars = km driven per day; battery bars = level %. Same window drives both, fetched from one new gateway API.
request: On the dashboard, show an odometer history bar chart (like Stitch) for the latest N days, with an easily-changeable day count (same number of bars) that also applies to battery level history. Odometer in kilometers. Likely needs a new API + a new port; the vehicle selector sends the Tesla ID. Read battery_range/battery_level/odometer from the latest X records of vehicle_snapshots. Build the chart bars (vanilla JS + a library if needed). Important library/architecture decisions must update the corresponding AGENTS.md.

decisions.decision: Window controlled at the gateway edge: telemetry port takes `since time.Time`; the gateway computes it from the `days` query param. Resolves tier-1 D1.
decisions.why: Brainstorm outcome; keeps the port a pure data accessor so every future consumer picks its own window, and makes the window 'sent to the API' as the user asked.

decisions.decision: Port method takes accountID; query filters account_id = $1 AND tesla_id = $2 (defense-in-depth). Resolves tier-1 D2.
decisions.why: Brainstorm outcome; belt-and-braces tenant isolation over a microsecond, even though the gateway already resolves tesla_id from the account's registered vehicles.

decisions.decision: No new index, no migration: the existing idx_vehicle_snapshots_vehicle_time (account_id, tesla_id, captured_at) already serves the ascending range scan. Tier 1 adds only a sqlc query + Reader method, so the database design gate does NOT trigger. Resolves tier-1 D3 and corrects the original proposal's 'one new index' assumption.
decisions.why: Verified against internal/telemetry/db/migrations/20260710000002_init_telemetry.sql; the index is ascending on captured_at with (account_id, tesla_id) as the leading exact-match columns.

decisions.decision: Safety LIMIT (e.g. 400) baked into the sqlc query as a guard against an oversized result if capture cadence increases. Resolves tier-1 D4.
decisions.why: Brainstorm outcome; cheap guard, the 30-day window already bounds normal results to ~30 rows.

decisions.decision: Odometer bars = km driven per day (delta = OdometerKm(dayN) - OdometerKm(dayN-1)). To render N delta bars the gateway fetches N+1 snapshots; days selector value = number of bars. Tooltip: date + km driven + cumulative odometer.
decisions.why: Brainstorm outcome; cumulative odometer bars are near-flat/dull, deltas match the Stitch varying-bars look and answer 'how much did I drive'.

decisions.decision: Battery bars = battery_level % (absolute 0-100, not a delta); tooltip: date + level% + rated range km.
decisions.why: Brainstorm outcome; battery level is naturally an absolute 0-100 series.

decisions.decision: Rendering = hand-rolled responsive SVG (Templ-generated, viewBox + width:100%, native <title> tooltips), NO chart library. Handler pre-computes heights + tooltip strings (no math in templates). A vanilla-JS chart lib is rejected for now.
decisions.why: Brainstorm outcome; best fit for the Node-less stack + simple bars and the most AI-efficient (no vendored asset, fully server-rendered). User asked for responsive charts; SVG scales natively.

decisions.decision: Important library/architecture decisions update the owning module's AGENTS.md in the same change. Tier 2 records the no-chart-lib decision in internal/gateway/AGENTS.md and adds a standing convention line requiring this for any client-side library / rendering-approach decision.
decisions.why: User's explicit ask; keeps durable architecture facts discoverable where an agent already looks.
